package_info.package_name: odio-illo-aut (example, representative of tea[.]xyz spam campaign)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package (and related packages) are part of a coordinated spam campaign to artificially inflate dependency counts for the tea[.]xyz crypto protocol, abusing npm and GitHub infrastructure for inauthentic engagement and potential crypto rewards. The packages are auto-generated, have no legitimate functionality, and are designed solely to game the 'proof of contribution' system.

execution_context.trigger: ci-cd (GitHub Actions workflow, on commit or scheduled cron)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
repository_dispatch:
  types: [commit-change]

jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: Publish to npm
        run: npm publish
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On commit or scheduled event, the workflow checks out the repository and publishes a new version of the package to npm, creating a new auto-generated package or version with artificial dependencies.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated publishing of thousands of packages/versions with no meaningful code, solely to inflate dependency counts, is a classic spam and abuse pattern.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal workflows automate legitimate CI/CD tasks, not mass package publication for inauthentic engagement.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate projects may use workflows to automate releases, but not at this scale or with this intent.
key_indicators: No meaningful code changes between versions
Triggering on every commit and on a daily cron schedule

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the package declares thousands of auto-generated dependencies, causing npm to resolve and install a massive, artificial dependency tree, inflating the package's perceived usage and contribution metrics.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate packages do not declare hundreds or thousands of meaningless dependencies, especially ones that are also auto-generated.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages declare only necessary dependencies; this behavior is designed to game metrics.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some monorepos or meta-packages may have many dependencies, but not at this scale or with this pattern.
key_indicators: Massive dependency trees with auto-generated names
Dependencies point to other spam packages
Presence of 'tea.yaml' or similar constitution files

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Copying README files from legitimate projects and embedding a 'tea.yaml' constitution is intended to deceive and game the tea[.]xyz protocol.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate projects have original documentation and meaningful constitutions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Forks or template-based projects may copy README files, but not for mass spam.
key_indicators: Presence of 'tea.yaml' in every spam repo
No real project activity or code

behavioral_signatures: Automated publishing of thousands of npm packages or versions in a short time frame
Packages with massive, auto-generated dependency trees
Presence of 'tea.yaml' or similar constitution files in every package
network_indicators: High-frequency npm publish events from the same user/org
Automated GitHub Actions activity tied to npm publishing
No external C2 or exfiltration, but high npm registry traffic
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for users or organizations publishing unusually high numbers of packages or versions in a short period, especially where package.json files declare hundreds or thousands of dependencies with auto-generated names. Flag repositories with 'tea.yaml' constitutions and copied README files from unrelated projects. Correlate with automated GitHub Actions workflows that trigger npm publish on every commit or on a daily schedule. Cross-reference with known spam orgs (e.g., vanthuanbt26, zitterorg, dramaorg) and look for patterns of inauthentic engagement or metric inflation.
